summary: Reproduced the concurrent pause/continue waiter collision in TokenizerWorker and fixed it by carrying a unique operation ID through the router broadcast and storing pending futures by operation ID. Added reverse-order concurrency, cancellation, dispatch-failure, and late-broadcast regressions.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before issue reproduction on the prepared base: operation identity was absent and the concurrent/boundary regression failed (3 failed, 1 passed). Raw output: reports/j-0b105fd3c373/raw/failing-before.txt

Passing-after worker regression including reverse broadcast ordering, cancellation cleanup, dispatch-failure cleanup, and late broadcast state application (10 passed). Raw output: reports/j-0b105fd3c373/raw/passing-focused.txt
Existing scheduler pause/continue boundary suite (21 passed). Raw output: reports/j-0b105fd3c373/raw/passing-scheduler-boundary.txt
Formatting tool availability only: the prepared interpreter does not contain ruff. git diff --check passed. Raw output: reports/j-0b105fd3c373/raw/ruff.txt and ruff-format.txt

gpu_execution_evidence: The defect and regression are asyncio/IPC control-plane behavior in TokenizerWorker; no GPU computation is involved, so no unrelated GPU smoke was used as evidence.
remaining_limitations: No full HTTP server or multi-process model-serving reproduction was run because model weights were not provided; the deterministic regression exercises the actual TokenizerWorker coroutine and broadcast implementation directly.
The test does not claim model semantic accuracy, distributed behavior, or GPU kernel validation.
Ruff was unavailable in the prepared Python environment; git diff --check passed.
